ApplicationSpec.description:
type discriminates which fields are required (spec §39):
python-wheel/jvm-jar carry a build artifact + a function/class entry
point; spark-declarative-pipeline carries a pipelineSpec reference
(a path to a spark-pipeline.yml, resolved through the same
artifact:// binding mechanism as `artifact`) instead — there is no
separate build artifact or single entry point for a declarative
pipeline, just its spec file and the transformation sources it
points at.
ApplicationSpec.title: ApplicationSpec

ExecutionProfileUpdate.description:
Same fields as Create minus `name` (identifies the resource via the
URL path, per REST PUT convention) — a full replace, not a partial
patch, matching how Terraform's own update model sends whole desired
state on every apply.
ExecutionProfileUpdate.title: ExecutionProfileUpdate

RequirementsSpec.description:
Explicit capability requirements (spec §20-21) a provider must
support for this workload to be schedulable there — matched against a
provider's CapabilitySet by control_plane/execution_provider.py's
match_capabilities(). All default False: most workloads need none of
these, and existing workload definitions parse unchanged.
RequirementsSpec.title: RequirementsSpec

WebhookSubscriptionOut.description:
secret is deliberately excluded — returned only once, implicitly,
at creation via the request the caller itself sent; never echoed
back by a GET, same discipline as credential_reference values never
round-tripping a raw secret (spec §35).
WebhookSubscriptionOut.title: WebhookSubscriptionOut

schema.title: Response List Artifact Bindings V1 Artifacts Get

get.description:
Export for SIEM ingestion (spec §36: "do not build a SIEM") —
filterable so an external system can pull incrementally rather than
re-reading the whole table. Operator+ only: the audit trail itself is
a privileged resource.

schema.title: Response List Audit Events V1 Audit Get

post.description:
Dynamic conformance comparison (spec §21) — resolves each run's
output location + storage credentials server-side and compares them
semantically (conformance/comparison.py). Read/verify-only, like
POST /v1/validate, so Analyst+ rather than Operator+.

get.description:
Provider certification report (spec §78) — every registered
execution+storage combination, PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED. Read-only, same
role as the rest of this router.

schema.title: Response List Dataset Bindings V1 Datasets Get
Response List Environments V1 Environments Get

put.description:
A NotFoundError here means either the environment itself or one of
its referenced profiles doesn't exist — both surface as 404, same as
every other resource's update in this file.

schema.title: Response List Execution Profiles V1 Execution Profiles Get

get.description:
Every registered ExecutionProfile/StorageProfile is a "provider"
instance in the UI sense (spec §32's Providers page) — there's no
separate provider-registry table, this just relabels the two profile
tables under one combined view.

schema.title: Response List Providers V1 Providers Get

get.description:
Read-only against the provider (a live capabilities() call), so —
like GET /v1/runs/{id}/logs and POST /v1/validate — answered
synchronously rather than deferred to the reconciler.

schema.title: Response List Runs V1 Runs Get

post.description:
Persists ACCEPTED and returns immediately — spec §24. No synchronous
provider call here; the reconciler (reconciler/service.py) picks this
run up asynchronously. Replaying the same Idempotency-Key returns the
existing run (200) rather than creating a duplicate (spec §25); a new
run is a fresh submission (202).

delete.description:
Records cancellation intent — reconciler/service.py's cancel_runs()
is what actually calls the provider (see run_service.cancel_run).

schema.title: Response List Run Events V1 Runs  Run Id  Events Get
Response List Storage Profiles V1 Storage Profiles Get

post.description:
Static, pre-submission capability check (spec §20-21) against an
inline workload definition — doesn't require the workload to already be
registered via POST /v1/workloads, matching `plane validate workload.yaml`'s
draft-checking use case.

schema.title: Response List Webhook Subscriptions V1 Webhooks Get

post.description:
Operator+ only — a webhook URL is effectively a place this server
sends run data, the same privilege level as cancel/environment
management (spec §67's own RBAC matrix).

schema.title: Response List Workloads V1 Workloads Get

post.description:
The request body is a portable workload definition (spec §7) — FastAPI
validates it against SparkWorkload before this handler ever runs.

get.description: Returns the latest version unless ?version= is given.

put.description:
version is a required query param (unlike GET, which defaults to
latest) — defaulting a destructive-ish full replace to "whichever is
latest" would be a surprising, dangerous default.
